first: चौ॰ – मुनि पाती पुलके दोउ भ्राता। अधिक सनेह समात न गाता॥
en: Hearing the letter, both brothers thrilled with a love too great for their bodies to hold. Seeing Bharata's pure love, the whole court felt special joy.

first: तब नृप दूत निकट बैठारे। मधुर मनोहर बचन उचारे॥
en: Then the king seated the messengers near him and spoke sweet, charming words: 'Brothers, tell me, are the two boys well? Have you seen them well with your own eyes?'

first: श्यामल गौर धरे धनु भाथा। बय-किसोर कैसिक मुनि साथा॥
en: 'One dark and one fair, carrying bows and quivers, young in age, with the sage Kaushika: do you know them? Tell me how they are.' Overcome by love, the king asked again and again.

first: जा दिन तैं मुनि गयउ लेवाई। तब तँ आजु साँचि सुधि पाई॥
en: 'Since the day the sage took them away, I have had true news of them only today. Tell me, how did Videha come to know them?' Hearing these loving words, the messengers smiled.

first: दो॰ – सुनहु महीपति मुकुट-मनि, तुम्ह सम धन्य न कोउ।
en: 'Listen, crown jewel of kings, no one is as blessed as you, whose sons are Rama and Lakshmana, both ornaments of the world.'

first: चौ॰ – पूछन जोग न तनय तुम्हारे। पुरुष-सिंह तिहुँ पुर उजियारे॥
en: 'Your sons need no asking about; they are lions among men, lighting up the three worlds. Before their fame and glory, the moon looks dim and the sun feels cool.'

first: तिन्ह कहँ कहिय नाथ किमि चीन्हे। देखिय रबि कि दीप कर लीन्हे॥
en: 'Master, how can you ask how they were recognised? Does one look at the sun with a lamp in hand? Many kings came to Sita's choosing of a husband, great warriors, each one greater than the last.'

first: सम्मु-सरासन काहु न टारा। हारे सकल बीर बरियारा॥
en: 'No one could move Shambhu's bow; all the mighty heroes were beaten. All the proud warriors in the three worlds had their strength broken by Shambhu's bow.'

first: सकइ उठाइ सरासुर मेरू। सेउ हिय हारि गयउ करि फेरू॥
en: 'Bana, who can lift Mount Meru, lost heart, walked round the bow and went away. Even Ravana, who playfully lifted Shiva's mountain, met defeat in that assembly.'

first: दो॰ – तहँ राम-रघुबंस-मनि, सुनिय महा-महिपाल।
en: 'There, great king, listen: Rama, jewel of the Raghu line, broke the bow without effort, as an elephant breaks a lotus stalk.'

first: सम्मु-सरासन काहु न टारा। हारे सकल बीर बरियारा॥
en: 'Not one of them could move Shambhu's bow, and all the strong heroes were defeated. The strength of every proud warrior in the three worlds was broken by that bow.'

first: सकइ उठाइ सरासुर मेरू। सेउ हिय हारि गयउ करि फेरू॥
en: 'Bana, able to lift Mount Meru, went round it and left, beaten at heart. Ravana, who lifted Shiva's mountain for fun, was also humbled in that assembly.'

first: दो॰ – तहँ राम-रघुबंस-मनि, सुनिय महा-महिपाल।
en: 'And there, hear this, great king: Rama, the jewel of the Raghu clan, broke the bow with no effort at all, as an elephant snaps a lotus stalk.'

first: चौ॰ – सुनि सरोष भृगुनायक आये। बहुत भाँति तिन्ह आँखि देखाये॥
en: 'Hearing of it, Parashurama came in anger and glared at them in many ways. Seeing Rama's strength, he gave him his own bow, and after many humble words he went to the forest.'

first: राजन राम अतुल बल जैसे। तेज-निधान लखन पुनि तैसे॥
en: 'King, as Rama has matchless strength, so is Lakshmana a treasure of glory. Kings tremble when he looks at them, as elephants do when a young lion looks.'

first: दो॰ – चलहु बेगि सुनि गुरु बचन, भलेहि नाथ सिर नाइ।
en: Hearing the guru's words, 'Go quickly,' the king bowed his head and said, 'Very well, master.' Then he went to the palace after giving the messengers lodging.

first: चौ॰ – राजा सब रनिवास बोलाई। जनक-पत्रिका बाँचि सुनाई॥
en: The king called all the women of the palace and read them Janaka's letter. Hearing the news, they were all glad, and the king told them the rest of the story.

first: प्रेम-प्रफुल्लित राजहि रानी। मनहुँ सिखिनि सुनि बारित बानी॥
en: The queens glowed with love, like peahens hearing the voice of the clouds. The wives of the elders gladly gave their blessings, and the mothers were lost in great joy.

first: लेहि परसपर अति प्रिय पाती। हृदय लगाइ जुड़ावहिँ छाती॥
en: They passed the dear letter to one another and held it to their hearts to soothe their breasts. The great king told again and again of the fame and deeds of Rama and Lakshmana.

first: मुनि प्रसाद कहि द्वार सिधाये। रानिन्ह तब महिदेव बोलाये॥
en: Saying it was all the sage's grace, he went out to the gate. Then the queens called the Brahmins and joyfully gave them gifts, and the Brahmins went away giving blessings.

first: सो-जाचक लिये हकारि, दीन्हि निछावर कोटि बिधि।
en: They called the beggars and gave them gifts in countless ways: 'Long live the four sons of the emperor Dasharatha!'

first: चौ॰ – कहत चले पहिरे पट नाना। हरषि हने गहगहे निसाना॥
en: Wearing many kinds of fine clothes, they went off saying this, and the great drums were beaten gladly. Everyone heard the news, and celebration began in every house.

first: भुवन चोरि-दस भरा उछाहू। जनकसुता-रघुधीर विधाहू॥
en: The fourteen worlds were filled with joy at the marriage of Janaka's daughter and the hero of the Raghus. Hearing the happy news, people were full of love and began to decorate the roads, houses and lanes.

first: जद्यपि अवध सदैव सुहावनि। रामपुरी मङ्गल-मय पावनि॥
en: Though Ayodhya is always lovely, being Rama's city, holy and full of blessings, still, as is the way of love, they made lovely festive decorations.

first: ध्वज पताक पट चामर चारू। छावा परम-विचित्र बजारू॥
en: Flags, banners, cloth and fine whisks covered the market most wonderfully. There were golden pitchers, arches, nets of gems, turmeric, durva grass, curd, rice and garlands.

first: दो॰ – मङ्गल भय निज निज भवन, लोगन्ह रचे बनाइ।
en: People decorated their own houses as homes of blessing; the streets were sprinkled with four kinds of fragrant water, and lovely designs were drawn in the courtyards.

first: चौ॰ – जहँ तहँ जूथन जूथ मिलि भामिनि। सजिनव-सपत सकल दुति दामिनि॥
en: Here and there women met in groups, all adorned and as bright as lightning; moon-faced and fawn-eyed, by their beauty they took away Rati's pride.

first: चौ॰ – भूप भरत पुनि लिये बोलाई। हय गय स्यन्दन साजहु जाई॥
en: Then the king called Bharata: 'Go and get the horses, elephants and chariots ready, and set out quickly with the wedding party of the hero of the Raghus.' Hearing this, both brothers thrilled with joy.

first: भरत सकल साहनी बोलाये। मायसु दीन्ह मुदित उठि धाये॥
en: Bharata called all the masters of the stables and gave them orders, and they rose gladly and ran. They put fine saddles on the horses, and fine horses of every colour shone.

first: सुभग सकल सुठि चञ्चल करनी। अय इव जरत धरत पग धरनी॥
en: All were lovely and very lively in their steps, setting their feet on the ground as if it were hot iron. There were many breeds beyond description, as if scorning the wind and wanting to fly.

first: तिन्ह सब छयल भये असवारा। भरत सरिस बय राजकुमारा॥
en: Fine young men, princes of Bharata's age, rode them all, all handsome and adorned, with arrows and bows in their hands and fine quivers at their waists.

first: दो॰ – छरे छबीले छैल सव, सूर सुजान नवीन।
en: All were slim, handsome and dashing, brave, skilled and young. With each rider went two foot soldiers, skilled in swordplay.

first: चौ॰ – चाँधे बिरद बीर रन गाढ़े। निकसि भये पुर बाहिर ठाढ़े॥
en: Heroes famed and steady in battle came out and stood outside the city. They put their clever horses through many paces and were glad to hear the drums and kettledrums.

first: बन्दि बिप्र सुर गुरु पितु माता। पाइ असीस मुदित सब भ्राता॥
en: Bowing to the Brahmins, gods, guru, father and mothers, all the brothers were glad to receive their blessings. The mothers looked lovingly at their faces, and they went to the gate with the king.

first: दो॰—कीन्ह सौच सब सहज सुचि, सरित पुनीत नहाइ।
en: The four brothers, pure by nature, washed and bathed in the holy river, did their morning rites and came to their father.

first: चौ॰—भूप विलोकि लिये उर लाई। बैठे हरषि रजायसु पाई॥
en: Seeing them, the king embraced them, and they sat down gladly when he allowed it. Seeing Rama, the whole court felt soothed, thinking it the highest reward for their eyes.

first: पुनि बसिष्ठ मुनि कौसिक आये। सुभग आसनन्हि मुनि बैठाये॥
en: Then the sages Vasishtha and Kaushika came, and the king seated them on fine seats. With his sons he worshipped them and touched their feet, and both gurus were filled with love on seeing Rama.

first: कहहिँ बसिष्ठ धरम इतिहासा। सुनहिँ महीस सहित रनिवासा॥
en: Vasishtha told stories of dharma, and the king listened with the women of the palace. Vasishtha gladly told in many ways the deeds of the son of Gadhi, which even sages' minds can hardly grasp.

first: बोले बामदेव सब साँची। कीरति कलित लोक तिहुँ माँची॥
en: Vamadeva said it was all true; his glorious fame had spread through the three worlds. Everyone was glad to hear it, and Rama and Lakshmana felt even greater joy.

first: दो॰—मङ्गल मोद उछाह नित, जाहिँ दिवस एहि भाँति।
en: Every day there was celebration, joy and gladness, and so the days passed. Ayodhya overflowed with happiness that grew more and more.

first: चौ॰—सुदिन सोधि कल कङ्कन छोरे। मङ्गल मोद बिनोद न थोरे॥
en: On a good day they untied the lovely wedding bands, with no small joy and merriment. Seeing the ever-new happiness, the gods felt envy and begged the Creator for birth in Ayodhya.

first: बिस्वामित्र चलन नित चहहीँ। राम-सप्रेम-विनय-बस रहहीँ॥
en: Every day Vishvamitra wanted to leave, but he stayed, held by Rama's loving, humble requests. Seeing the king's devotion grow a hundredfold each day, the great king of sages praised him.

first: माँगत बिदा राउ अनुरागे। सुतन्ह समेत ठाढ़ भये आगे॥
en: When he asked leave, the king was moved with love and stood before him with his sons: 'Master, all this wealth is yours; I am your servant, with my sons and wives.'

first: करब सदा लरिकन पर छोहू। दरसन देत रहब मुनि मोहू॥
en: 'Always be kind to the boys, and keep giving me your sight, sage.' Saying this, the king with his sons and queens fell at his feet and could not speak.

first: दीन्हि असीस बिप्र बहु भाँती। चले न प्रीति रीति-कहि जाती॥
en: The Brahmin sage blessed them in many ways and set out; his love cannot be told. Rama, lovingly, with all his brothers, went with him a long way and came back only when given leave.

first: दो॰—राम-रूप भूपति-भगति, ब्याह-उछाह-अनन्द।
en: Thinking of Rama's beauty, the king's devotion and the joy of the wedding, the moon of Gadhi's clan went away gladly, praising them in his heart.

first: चौ॰—बामदेव-रघुकुल गुरु ज्ञानी। बहुरि गाधि-सुत कथा बखानी॥
en: Vamadeva and the wise guru of the Raghu clan again told the story of the son of Gadhi. Hearing his fame again and again, the king praised in his heart the power of his own merit.

first: बहुरे लोग राजयसु भयऊ। सुतन्ह समेत नृपति गृह गयऊ॥
en: At the king's word the people went home, and the king went to his palace with his sons. Everywhere people sang of Rama's wedding, and his holy fame spread over the three worlds.

first: आये ब्याहि राम घर जन तें। बसे अनन्द अवध सब तब तें॥
en: Ever since Rama came home married, every kind of joy has lived in Ayodhya. Even Sarasvati and the king of serpents cannot describe the joy of the Lord's wedding.

first: कबि-कुल-जीवन पावन जानी। राम-सीय-जस मंगल-खानी॥
en: Knowing that the fame of Rama and Sita is the life of poets, holy and a mine of blessings, I have told a little of it to make my own speech pure.

first: निज गिरा पावनि करन कारन, राम-जस तुलसी कह्यो।
en: To make his own speech pure, Tulsi has told Rama's fame; the story of the hero of the Raghus is an endless ocean, and what poet has reached its far shore? Those who hear with respect and sing of the joyful sacred thread and wedding ceremonies will always find happiness by the grace of Vaidehi and Rama.

first: सो॰—सिय रघुबीर बिबाह, जे सप्रेम गावहिँ सुनहि।
en: Those who lovingly sing and hear of the wedding of Sita and the hero of the Raghus will always have joy, for Rama's fame is a home of blessings.
